full_judgment:
9. The plaintiffs filed 11 rent receipts Exhibits 1-1(K) showing payment of rents to the ex-landlord in respect of the suit land. The trial Court, as it appears, observed that the plaintiff No.1 who is PW 1 and son of Saku Sarder and PW 2 who is son of Hossain Sarder deposed in this case in support of their plaint case in respect of title and possession ill the suit land by way of inheritance from their predecessors-in-interest and they totally denied the defendants' case and their documents brought on record by their evidence. They further asserted that they have been in continuous possession of the suit land from the time of their predecessors and the defendants never possessed the suit land at any point of time. PW 3 Md Ayezuddin Mondal, PW 4 Taser Mondal, PW 5 Iman Mondal, PW 6 Shamsul Alam and PW 7 Khoda Box deposed in support of the plaintiffs' case in respect of title and possession of suit land for more than 12 years. 

 10. The trial Court observed that, "All of these five witnesses are owners of contiguous lands of the suit land and they have produced documents of their title in support of their statements. They have produced the Mouza Map Exhibit 12 to show that, in fact, they have got land adjacent to the suit land. Exhibits 8-8(b), Exhibit 9, Exhibits 10-10(c), Exhibits 11(a)-11(b) and Exhibit 12 are the title deeds, rent receipts and rent rolls, etc. of the supporting witnesses namely, PWs 3-7 which prove that these persons, in fact, do own and possess lands adjacent to some of the suit plots as claimed by them. From the evidence of these witnesses it is difficult to deny the plaintiffs' claim of possession of the suit land from the time of their predecessors. But again, the trial Court observed that on consideration of both oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case reason fails to believe that the plaintiffs continued to hold their title and possession in the suit land against the claim of the contesting defendants. The trial Court, it may be stated here, did not mention what other facts and circumstances and evidence, the Court considered in arriving at the conclusion that reason fails to believe that the plaintiffs continued to hold their title and possession in the suit land in the face of evidence of PWs 3-7 who, according to the trial Court, are contiguous owners' of land of the suit land. 

 12. The defendants during trial put forward a new plea that after the institution of the suit, the plaintiffs took forcible possession of the suit land in 1976 when the defendants' prayer for temporary injunction was vacated. It is undisputed that the defendants did not inform this broad fact to the trial Court by filing a petition. They also did not prove their alleged date of dispossession by the plaintiffs and the first date of taking possession by their predecessor-in-interest Tayebuddin Biswas from the plaintiffs' predecessors. The trial Court further observed that from the recitals of the deed dated 5th Ashar, 1341 BS in favour of Tayebuddin Biswas, predecessor-in-interest of the defendants, executed by Saku Sarder and Hossain Sarder, predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiffs, it appears that this is not a title deed. The trial Court further observed that the genuineness of the deed of relinquishment Exhibit F and the solenama having not been proved by calling for the original record of the criminal case these can be relied upon, especially in view of categorical denial by the plaintiffs. Without going into merit of the solenama it cannot be safely said that solenama in a criminal case can be treated as a title deed in a properly framed civil suit, specially in view of the fact that the execution of the solenama was strongly denied by the plaintiffs. The learned Advocate for the plaintiffs contended that the deed of. relinquishment does not confer title and this document being one over Taka 100 should have been registered as per provisions of Registration Act and for want of registration, the same is not a valid document. It is also undisputed that the document was not impounded as per provisions of Stamp Act. The trial Court and the High Court Division held that the contesting defendants have filed rent receipts Exhibits A-A(28) showing payment of rents to the ex-landlords and rent receipts Exhibits A(29)-A(49) showing payment of rent for the suit land to the Government Acquired Estate for the suit land and these go to prove their possession. 

 14. Regarding the dakhilas the Court of appeal below held that by dakhilas Exhibits A (9)-A(17) the defendants are found to have paid rents in the names of Saku Sarder and Hossain Sarder. That means the names of Saku Sarder and Hossain Sarder stand recorded in the dakhilas as tenants. The Court of appeal further held that most of these dakhilas are of the years 1341 BS and the dakhila Exhibit A(9) is of the year 1352 BS and had Tayebuddin's name been mutated in the landlord's sherista immediately after execution of alleged document, Exhibit F as claimed by defendants, they would not have paid rents in the names of Saku Sarder and Hossain Sarder by these dakhilas Exhibits A(9)-A(17). The appellate Court further held that the SA khatians Exhibits D(2) and D(3) show that names of defendant No.1 and Gafuran Nessa were recorded in the Khatian but the dakhilas Exhibits A(35)-A(39)are in the name of Tayebuddin. When Tayebuddin was not recorded tenant in the SA khatian how the rent can be put in his name instead of the recorded tenant. For all these reasons, the Court of appeal came to the conclusion that all these dakhilas were managed by defendant No.1 who was a Government Kanongo.
